readerTitle: Starbucks changed what earns a star, and chose which customers to keep
caseNote: 실제 기업 (Starbucks Rewards 2016년 적립 방식 변경) + 가상 적용 (포장재 유통업체). 3번 카드의 음료 가격은 설명용 가상 수치
insight: 로열티 프로그램이 무엇을 세느냐(방문, 금액, 주문 수)가 어떤 고객에게 돈을 써서 붙잡을지를 결정한다.
misconception: 로열티 프로그램은 모든 단골에게 똑같이 고마움을 표시하는 중립적인 장치다.

sources.text: Starbucks Stories & News, Starbucks Rewards program changes announcement (February 2016; changes effective April 2016)
News coverage of customer reaction to the 2016 change (e.g., CNBC, The Wall Street Journal, February 2016)
Starbucks Stories & News, tiered Rewards redemption announcement (2019) and Rewards redemption changes (February 2023)
Starbucks annual reports (Form 10-K) and earnings releases: Rewards membership, share of U.S. sales, mobile order and stored value

factChecks.note: 2016년 이전 구조(구매 1건당 별 1개, Gold 회원은 별 12개에 무료 음료 1잔)와 2016년 4월 이후 구조(1달러당 별 2개, 별 125개에 무료 음료 또는 음식)를 Starbucks 2016년 2월 발표문으로 확인하세요.
고객이 별을 더 모으려고 주문을 나눠 결제했다는 내용은 2016년 당시 언론 보도와 Starbucks 설명에 널리 나옵니다. 카드에는 'widely reported'로 적었습니다. 원문 표현을 확인하세요.
Rewards 회원이 미국 직영 매장 매출에서 차지하는 비중은 구체 수치를 쓰지 않고 'a large share'로만 적었습니다. 게시 전 최신 10-K나 실적 발표로 확인하세요.
2019년 단계별 교환 도입과 2023년 일부 보상의 필요 별 개수 인상, 그에 대한 고객 불만 보도를 확인하세요. 카드에는 구체 수치 없이 적었습니다.

cards.title: Starbucks changed what earns a star, and chose which customers to keep
body: In 2016, Starbucks changed one rule in its rewards program: what gets counted.

Before, every purchase earned a star, whether it was a cheap coffee or a big order for the office. After, stars followed dollars. Some of its most frequent customers were angry. Starbucks kept the change anyway.

image.label: A coffee cup on a counter with a tally of stars beside it
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 카운터 위에 테이크아웃 컵 하나, 옆에 별 스티커 도장판. 한쪽은 '방문 횟수' 체크 표시, 다른 쪽은 '동전 더미'로 바뀌는 모습. 실제 로고, 사이렌 마크, 브랜드 색상은 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: It's 2015. Your program counts visits.
body: Members earn one star per purchase. Twelve stars earn a free drink. It's widely reported that some customers pay for each item separately to collect more stars, and lines slow down. Meanwhile, a customer who buys a big order gets the same star as someone buying one small coffee.

options.text: Keep one star per visit, but limit how often stars can be earned
options.feedback: This stops order-splitting and keeps your daily regulars happy. But big spenders still get no more than anyone else.

options.text: Switch to stars per dollar spent
options.feedback: Rewards line up with revenue and splitting orders stops working. The cost: frequent customers with small orders now earn far more slowly.

options.text: Keep stars per visit and add bonus stars for large orders
options.feedback: You try to reward both groups. The rules get harder to explain, and gaming moves to whatever threshold the bonus uses.

choice.afterReveal: Starbucks chose B. From April 2016, members earned 2 stars per dollar, and a free drink or food item took 125 stars.

cards.title: Same rule change, opposite effects.
body: Take two loyal customers with made-up prices. The small-order regular now needs about twice as many visits for a reward. The big spender needs slightly fewer.
cards.softwareNote: Software has the same choice. Rewarding logins favors frequent light users. Rewarding seats or usage favors big accounts. Neither is neutral.

cards.title: What you count is who you keep.
body: A loyalty program is a budget you spend on keeping certain customers. The **unit of reward**, whether visits, dollars or items, decides which customers get that budget.

Counting visits rewards frequency. Counting dollars rewards spending. Starbucks decided spending was the behavior worth paying for. It accepted that some daily, low-spend regulars would feel they had lost out.

image.label: Two scales: one weighs visits, one weighs dollars
image.brief: 두 개의 저울 인포그래픽. 왼쪽 저울은 'Visits' 라벨, 작은 컵 여러 개가 올라가 무거움. 오른쪽 저울은 'Dollars' 라벨, 큰 주문 봉투 하나가 무거움. 브랜드 로고 없음.

cards.title: The stars weren't the whole program.
body: Rewards lived inside the Starbucks app, next to mobile ordering and a prepaid balance. Members could order ahead, skip the line and pay without a wallet. Each feature made the next visit easier.
Starbucks regularly reports that Rewards members account for **a large share** of its U.S. store sales. Any rival can hand out points. A morning habit built around an app is much harder to copy.

cards.title: Every rule change spends trust.
body: Customers judge new rules against the old ones, so any cut feels like a loss. Starbucks reworked how rewards are redeemed in 2019 and raised the stars needed for several rewards in 2023. Each change drew public complaints.

Frequency also has value that dollars miss. A daily customer who spends little keeps the habit alive and may bring friends. And people learn to game any rule you choose, so watch what the new rule invites.

cards.title: Now it's a packaging distributor.
body: You supply boxes and tape to local manufacturers. Your loyalty program gives a fixed credit on every order. Customers have started placing many small orders, and each one costs you a delivery run.
What should the program count instead?

options.text: Keep the per-order credit, but cap it per month
options.feedback: The cap limits the damage quickly. But small orders still earn the same as full ones, so the costly behavior stays.

options.text: Rebate on yearly volume, with a bonus for full-pallet orders
options.feedback: You reward both the spending and the order size that keep your delivery costs down. Expect complaints from small customers, so explain the change early.

options.text: Drop the program and lower prices for everyone
options.feedback: It ends the gaming, but you lose a tool for shaping behavior. Your best customers get nothing extra for staying.

cards.title: Decide which behavior you're paying for before you reward it.
body: Every loyalty rule favors some customers over others. Choose the behavior you want more of, then accept who loses out.
**Try it today:** pick one reward you offer, whether a discount, a rebate or a team bonus. Write down what it actually counts and who earns the most under it.
